idiom_name: hand-written per-struct DAO over the SQLite C API (sqlite3_prepare_v2 / bind / step)
implementation_notes: C has no ORM and no column inheritance, so the pattern is written literally: one struct per concrete type, one table per struct with the base fields repeated as ordinary columns, and one DAO of prepared statements per table built with sqlite3_prepare_v2, sqlite3_bind_* and sqlite3_column_*. What replaces the classic structure is discipline rather than an idiom - a shared struct header as the first member so generic code can touch the base fields, a migration script per table, and a UNION ALL statement (with NULL padding and a literal type tag) for hierarchy-wide reads. Keeping the embedded base struct as the first member is still worth it even though the table duplicates the columns, because it lets shared code operate on base fields without copying.
pitfalls: Key uniqueness is yours to enforce: with one AUTOINCREMENT per table two concrete rows can share a key value, so use a shared key table or application-generated ids before reading the tables as one hierarchy.
SQLITE_STATIC keeps the pointer instead of copying it - a bound string must outlive sqlite3_step, or you bind freed memory.
Repeating base columns by hand invites drift: nothing in the C type system ties engineers.name to managers.name.
